items.title: 61539_Butter Jackson oral history interview
items.q: I didn't hear him but once and then later on I heard him on a record

ctx.x: Yeah.-- and Sidney DeParis. Now, Shirley Clay, he got him from Earl Hines. And the trombones was Claude Jones and Bennie Morton and myself. And the saxophones was Rupert Cole and Edward Inge and Bob Carroll and, of course, Don himself. And Horace Henderson was on piano.

items.title: 61539_Butter Jackson oral history interview
items.q: But that's who I first heard that impressed me was Earl "Fatha" Hines. He was playing a style of piano then that was way ahead, way ahead of his time.

ctx.x: That's right. But his name, Louis; they said Louie, you know. But that's who I first heard that impressed me was Earl "Fatha" Hines. He was playing a style of piano then that was way ahead, way ahead of his time. And I didn't hear him no more until I heard him on the records with
Louie. He made records with Louie. But I heard him then and he was with this orchestra out of Pittsburgh.

items.title: 61539_Butter Jackson oral history interview
items.q: I took some lessons from him.

ctx.x: So then they went -- they had me go to a teacher. His name was Professor [Brane.]
And I took some lessons from him. He was all right but I didn't like him. I didn't like his approach, [because]a kid, you know, a kid, if you don't approach a kid right, you'll get nothing from him.
